title: Functions: Counting, Injections, Surjections and Bijections
quickIdea: Total functions are n to the m. Injections are falling factorials, surjections are inclusion-exclusion or n! times a Stirling number, and bijections exist only when the sizes match.
remember: A function from A to B assigns to every a in A exactly one b in B; the set of such functions has cardinality |B| to the |A|.
A function is injective (one-to-one) when different inputs have different outputs; it is surjective (onto) when every element of the codomain is hit; bijective when both.
The number of injections from an m-element set to an n-element set is n(n-1)...(n-m+1) = n!/(n-m)!, and 0 when m > n.
The number of surjections from m elements onto n elements is the alternating sum of C(n,k)(n-k)^m over k, which equals n! times S(m, n), and 0 when m < n.
The number of bijections from an n-element set to itself is n!.
Cardinality decides possibility: an injection needs m <= n, a surjection needs m >= n, and a bijection needs m = n.
The image of a function is a subset of the codomain, and surjective means image equals codomain. Confusing range with codomain is the classic error.
A function from A to B is a relation from A to B in which every element of A appears exactly once as a first coordinate, so the n to the m count is a subset of the 2 to the (m n) relations.
Proving injectivity is usually done in the contrapositive form: assume f(x) = f(y) and derive x = y.

example.prompt: How many functions are there from a 4-element set to a 3-element set, how many are injective, how many surjective, how many bijective?
example.work: Total is 3 to the 4 = 81. Injective is 0 because 4 > 3. Surjective is 81 - 3 times 16 + 3 times 1 - 0 = 81 - 48 + 3 = 36. Bijective is 0 because the sizes differ.

gateAngle: GATE CS 2015 Set 2 Q.40 is exactly this count: the number of onto functions from {1,2,3,4} to {a,b,c} is 36, and the two standard routes are inclusion-exclusion and 3! times S(4,3).

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: See GATE CS 2015 Set 2 Q.40 in the linked PYQs.
variations.why: Inclusion-exclusion gives 81 - 48 + 3 = 36, and the same number comes from 3! times S(4,3) = 6 times 6.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: How many injective functions are there from a 4-element set to a 6-element set, and how many from a 6-element set to a 4-element set?
variations.why: The first is a falling factorial with four factors. The second is impossible because an injection cannot exist from a larger set into a smaller one.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: How many functions from a 3-element set to a 3-element set are neither injective nor surjective?
variations.why: The total is 3 to the 3 = 27. Injections number 3 times 2 times 1 = 6 and surjections also number 6, and on equal finite sets those two classes coincide (they are the 6 bijections). So the functions that are neither are 27 - 6 = 21.

trap.what: Using |B| to the |A| for onto functions, or forgetting that a surjection is impossible when the domain is smaller than the codomain.
trap.why: The power counts all functions, most of which miss elements. Surjectivity needs inclusion-exclusion (or Stirling numbers) because the condition is 'no element of B is missed', which is a union of bad events.
trap.counterexample: From a 2-element set to a 3-element set there are 9 functions and none is onto: two inputs can hit at most two of the three outputs.

check.question: How many bijections are there from a 5-element set to itself?
check.explanation: A bijection is a permutation of the set, so the count is 5! = 120.
